newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Ashland fire keeps Midco hot.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Ashland fire keeps Midco hot.

text.p: A fire at Ashland Inc's refinery in Minnesota kept the focus on midcontinent refined products markets Monday while markets in Houston and New York Harbor were relatively mellow early on, traders said.
Underlying futures markets were moving down in light trade following action in crude oil pits, where players were rolling June positions into July ahead of June crude's expiry Tuesday.

Group Three unleaded differentials jumped Monday morning as the market digested news of the fire Friday at Ashland's 70,000 barrel per day Minnesota refinery. Unleaded differentials rose a half cent over NYMEX gasoline to between 7.00 cents and 7.50 cents a gallon.
"There was talk all this morning about the fire. The market seems a bit inflated," said a Group Three trader.
Other products were talked largely steady from Friday, with Group Three low sulphur offered at 6.00 cent over NYMEX heat.

GASOLINE: Action was light with differentials coming in a touch softer in the early going, traders said. Prompt M2 regular conventional was assessed at between 2.25 and 2.00 cents under June NYMEX unleaded, while "A2" regular reformulated blend was offered at a 1.00 cent over June NYMEX.
DISTILLATES: Heating oil and low sulphur diesel assessments were in line with Friday's levels, but a tug-of-war looked like it was taking shape on the jet fuel front.
Some players were reporting numbers for prompt 54-grade as low as 0.75 cent over June futures, but others still saw differentials at Friday's levels of about 1.25 cents over.

Markets were looking very steady despite news Phillips Petroleum will not have its Sweeny, Texas refinery fully restored after a power failure last Tuesday until between May 21-25 or about three days behind schedule.
Prompt "M1" regular convention was still talked at about 3.50 cents under the June print, traders said.

"A1" regular reformulated still stood at the firm levels achieved cent last week to offers of about 0.15 cent under the NYMEX. The shutdown of Phillips' Sweeny Texas refinery on May 12 and the fire at Citgo's Corpus Christi alkylation unit led to the bullish move, traders said.
